messages.author: d05aff47543a426f
messages.subject: Support for circular distributions
parts:
Hi everyone, I'm contributing some circular probability distributions, starting with von mises. You can find the work I've done so far in the 'circular' branch.

Does anyone have any thoughts on choosing the support for circular distributions? I was thinking (-pi,pi), but I the R 'circular' package seems to use (0,2pi).

I also wonder if, given von_mises_log(y, mu, kappa), I should use something like fmod to silently translate y and mu to the support interval, or if it would be better to issue an error.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Support for circular distributions
parts:
On Tuesday, October 30, 2012 3:41:00 PM UTC-4, Daniel Mitchell wrote:
Does anyone have any thoughts on choosing the support for circular distributions? I was thinking (-pi,pi), but I the R 'circular' package seems to use (0,2pi).

IMO, it is up to you if the computational considerations are the same either way. If I were doing it, I would follow the convention in the circular package but that is just because I do almost everything in R. Is there another software package that people often use for circular distributions? The only thing I would say is to have all of the circular distributions you plan to implement follow the same convention, whatever that may be, unless there is a good reason to depart from that.
I also wonder if, given von_mises_log(y, mu, kappa), I should use something like fmod to silently translate y and mu to the support interval, or if it would be better to issue an error.

Here, I think that an exception should be thrown outside the support and have the message mention the correct bounds. If we permit unrestricted input and do some mod thing internally, then the posterior is technically improper, right?

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Support for circular distributions
parts:
On 10/30/12 6:52 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> On Tuesday, October 30, 2012 3:41:00 PM UTC-4, Daniel Mitchell wrote:

> I also wonder if, given von_mises_log(y, mu, kappa), I should use something like fmod to silently translate y and mu
> to the support interval, or if it would be better to issue an error.
>
> Here, I think that an exception should be thrown outside the support and have the message mention the correct bounds. If
> we permit unrestricted input and do some mod thing internally, then the posterior is technically improper, right?

For now, you should implement it like the other distributions.

We may make wholesale changes to them at some point, because
we're in the middle of rethinking the following behaviors:

- prob functions (pdf, pmf) with variates out of bound
- prob functions with parameters out of bounds
- cumulative distribution functions with params out of bounds
- cumulative distributions with variates out of support

- same again at limits of support or parameter definendess (e.g., scale = 0)

and whether to just:

- return NaN
- return -infinity
- raise an exception

None of this really matters for Stan models as they all have the
same effect of causing the current position to be Metropolis
rejected by the sampler.

- Bob
